ledger.note: 1867: Russia forms the Turkestan Governor-Generalship at Tashkent. Infobox 'Established: 23 July 1867'; 'initially consisted of two oblasts (provinces), Syr-Darya Oblast and Semirechye Oblast'; RC: 'In July 1867, a new Province of Turkestan was created' under Kaufmann.

region.text: Zeravshan Okrug (1868), later Samarkand Oblast: Samarkand and the upper Zeravshan

ledger.note: 1868: Samarkand and the Zeravshan valley pass to Russia. 'the city surrendered without resisting (May 1868)'; the peace of 5 July 1868 cost Bukhara Samarkand; RT: 'In 1868, the Zeravshan Okrug was formed from annexed Bukharan territory', reorganised into Samarkand Oblast in 1887.

region.text: the Emirate of Bukhara after the loss of Samarkand

ledger.note: 1868: Bukhara becomes a Russian protectorate. The 5 July 1868 treaty left Bukhara a semi-independent vassal; RT: the governorate-general 'excluded the Russian protectorates of the Emirate of Bukhara and the Khanate of Khiva' whose 'independence was largely nominal'. Cliopatria has no Bukhara shape for 1868-1917.

region.text: Amu Darya Division (1873), centre Petro-Aleksandrovsk, annexed from Khiva

ledger.note: 1873: the Amu Darya Division is annexed from Khiva. 'To these were added in 1873 the Amu Darya Division', 'annexed from the Khanate of Khiva'. The month (August, treaty) is in the khanate-of-khiva dossier, not on this page.

region.text: the Khanate of Khiva after the loss of the Amu Darya Division

ledger.note: 1873: Khiva becomes a Russian protectorate. 'on 4 June, the Khan sued for peace'; 'The Khanate of Khiva became a Russian protectorate.' Cliopatria draws no Khiva shape for 1873-1917.

region.text: Fergana Oblast (1876), the rump of the Kokand Khanate

ledger.note: 1876: Kokand is abolished and the Fergana Oblast formed. 'in 1876 the Fergana Oblast, formed from the remaining rump of the Kokand Khanate'; RC: 'Fergana Oblast was created in its place'.
1882: Semirechye passes to the Steppe governor-generalship. 'part of Russian Turkistan between 1867 and 1882'; then Steppe, 1882-1899. Verny (Almaty) goes with it.

1886: the governor-generalship is also called the Turkestan Krai. 'It was formally organized as the Turkestan Governor-Generalship in 1867, and was also known as the Turkestan Krai from 1886 onward.' Same state, same colour.

1897: the Transcaspian Oblast joins the governor-generalship. RT: 'In 1897, the Transcaspian Oblast' incorporated; RC dates the oblast itself to May 1881 (annexed after Geok Tepe, December 1880) and Merv to 16 March 1884, under the Russian Empire. The transfer is administrative; the page does not name the body it came from.
1899: Semirechye returns to Turkestan. 'again between 1899 and 1917' in Russian Turkistan; its seat Verny. The 1882-99 gap is the Steppe governor-generalship's.

1918: the Turkestan republic replaces the governor-generalship; whether Bukhara's protectorate (and Khiva's, below) passed to it is on no page (the TASSR page 'does not describe their relationship'). The emirate falls in 1920 (emirate-of-bukhara dossier). Bridged here so that the pair closes.
1918: as for Bukhara; the khanate falls in February 1920 (khanate-of-khiva dossier). Bridged so that the pair closes; the page is silent on Khiva and the TASSR.

wars.outcome: Russian victory: Kokand abolished (1876), Bukhara and Khiva made protectorates (1868, 1873), Transcaspia annexed (1881-84); the Afghan frontier delimited after Panjdeh (1885).
wars.note: The war is Russian-Empire-wide; the dates inside this state's life (1867 on) are the Zeravshan, Amu Darya, Fergana and Transcaspian steps.

wars.name: Central Asian revolt of 1916
wars.outcome: Suppressed; 'Order had not fully been restored by the time the February Revolution took place in 1917.' No border changed.
wars.note: 'sparked by a decree issued on 25 June 1916' (the labour conscription); zones not on the page.

certainty.note: Steppe and desert frontiers; the Chinese frontier follows the 1864 Treaty of Tarbagatai ('roughly set the current Chinese-Kazakh border', RC) and the Bukhara and Khiva lines are approximate.
The Afghan frontier was delineated 1885-86 after Panjdeh (RC) and the Pamirs border was settled in the 1890s; the Bukhara and Khiva protectorate lines stay approximate.

notes:
Written for batch ia-03-x from five pages (budget 2-5): Russian Turkestan, Russian conquest of Central Asia, Semirechye Oblast, Syr-Darya Oblast, Turkestan ASSR. A colony-type dossier: Cliopatria has no row; its land lies inside the Russian Empire row (bbox reaches 35.19 N from 1873) and the Emirate of Bukhara and Khanate of Khiva rows stop in 1867/1872 and resume in 1918.
Counterparts: gains name the former owner (bukhara, khiva, kokand), whose own dossiers record the matching loss to russian-empire, the sovereign; the vassal events name the protectorates as the vassals. Where an oblast moved between governor-generalships the counterpart is the name 'Governor-Generalship of the Steppes' (no dossier; an administrative unit).
Disagreements: RT says the Transcaspian Oblast joined in 1897 (other works say 1899; not opened); SDO lists the Amu Darya Okrug among the six original uyezds although RT adds it in 1873; SO gives Semirechye's creation as 1854 in the body and 23 July 1867 in the infobox; SDO's area is 504,700 km2 in the infobox with a body figure that does not agree.
Not on the pages opened: the 1871-1881 Russian occupation of the Ili (Kuldja) valley (belongs with the Ili Sultanate and the Qing), the Pamir posts (1891-95) and the boundaries of the uyezds. Counterparts needing dossiers: tekke-turkmen (Transcaspian oasis peoples, 1879-84), turkestan-assr (written in this batch).
